issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual API) requires Stock to provide a method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). The template Stock implementation, however, defines addItem(StockIngredient) instead, while the solution uses addToStockIngredients. This name/signature mismatch between the UML/specification and the template will confuse students: they may implement SealSaloon expecting addToStockIngredients (as specified) but the template Stock does not expose it, causing compile errors or forcing students to change the provided Stock class in ways not described by the task.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the specification: rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or add an alias addToStockIngredients that calls addItem). Ensure the method name in the template, UML/problem text, and tests are consistent so students implement against the expected API.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) but the template Stock class provides addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This naming mismatch for the same operation (adding a StockIngredient to the stock) creates a mapping barrier: students reading the specification will look for addToStockIngredients while the starter code exposes addItem, potentially causing confusion and compilation/test failures if instructors/tests rely on the diagram name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) to match the problem statement and solution. Alternatively, add a new wrapper method public void addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient ingredient) { addItem(ingredient); } so both names are available while preserving existing template behavior.
